s.t: Alice Costelloe says the song's closing affirmation was a deliberate choice, inspired by a quote from Feist about repetition becoming a kind of spell.
s.q: a deliberate choice; inspired by a quote from Feist about repetition becoming a kind of spell

s.t: Alice Costelloe admits the song’s positive ending is “unbearably cheesy”, but says she wanted a moment that could “manifest something more positive”.
s.q: unbearably cheesy; manifest something more positive

s.t: Alice Costelloe’s ‘How Can I’ was produced by Mike Lindsay in his studio in Margate.
s.q: Produced by Mike Lindsay in his Margate studio

f.t: She bought a £60 flute on Amazon and taught herself to play it; encouraged by producer Mike Lindsay, she used it on every track of Move On With The Year.
f.q: she bought a £60 flute on Amazon and taught herself how to play it. Encouraged by producer Mike Lindsey, the flute quickly became central to the record, appearing on every track.

f.t: She spent years in the 2010s as one half of the duo Big Deal, a transatlantic project with Kacey Underwood.
f.q: Years of playing in the duo Big Deal (her 2010s Transatlantic project with Kacey Underwood)

f.t: She had only a six-month window in which to make her album, Move On With The Year.
f.q: But with only a six-month window in which to make the album, something had to give.
